detail.longDescription: FPGAs are general purpose and can be made to do anything. They are basically a function of the number of repeated elements. They are "commodity items" except for one fact. The current FPGA manufacturers won't disclose the details of the design internals to "protect their intellectual property". Only small FPGAs have been reverse engineered and there are some high-quality tools that have been developed. Their limitation is information. Because of high costs set by the big players the ability to build truly complex FPGA designs (e.g. an NVIDIA competitor or an ARM competitor or a high-function inference chip) is "closed source information" limited. But by design FPGAs are basicaly simple repeated elements that can be scaled to any size. That means that a new open sourced chip could be a range from really tiny to enormous with cost purely a function of chip die area. This makes it a pure commodity play. Some "bright spot" student wanting to start a company could get funded to create a new FPGA design (e.g. since wires take up most of the area figure out how to put the wires "under the logic" in a multi-layer design). Extend existing open-source software tools chains for the new chip design. Open-source the design and license it which is what made ARM so big. Within hours I'm certain the FPGA tools would be updated to full support of the new chip, opening the market to real, high powered chips. Or create your own open-source tools. Build the company around selling expertise like consulting on custom board-level designs using the new chips. Turning highly capable FPGAs into volume chips is a market nobody has addressed. What it needs is someone who wants to be a startup CEO and someone who has capital to create the first design (probably a few million dollars). Of course if you have access to REAL capital then buy Xilinx or Altera and open source their design and tool chain. The company that doesn't get bought would disappear overnight. (Somebody call Musk with the idea :-) ) If you know someone who wants to "go big fast" either path is a major opportunity.
